# netbox_inventory_items (Data Source)

Lists inventory_item objects matching the given filters.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "netbox_inventory_items" "test" {
  filters = [
    { name = "name", value = "test-inventory_item" },
  ]
}
```

Repeating a name sends that parameter once per value. Custom fields filter as cf_<field name>, e.g. cf_tier, with the field's own filter logic: loose is a case-insensitive substring match, exact an exact match. NetBox ignores names it has no custom field for, and such an entry does not narrow the result. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters))
- `limit` (Number) The maximum number of objects to return from the API lookup. Defaults to 1000.

### Read-Only

- `inventory_items` (Attributes List) The matching inventory_items. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--inventory_items))

<a id="nestedatt--filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the query filter (the API list parameter).
- `value` (String) Value to filter by.


<a id="nestedatt--inventory_items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `inventory_items`

Read-Only:

- `asset_tag` (String) Unique asset tag.
- `component_id` (Number) Id of the device component named by component_type.
- `component_type` (String) Type of the device component the item is bound to, e.g. dcim.interface. Requires component_id.
- `created` (String)
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values by field name. Every value is a string; NetBox coerces numbers and booleans. An object field holds the related object's id, e.g. "12", a multiobject field a JSON list of ids in any order, e.g. jsonencode([12, 13]). A key removed from the map is cleared in NetBox (set {} to clear all).
- `description` (String)
- `device_id` (Number) Id of the device.
- `discovered` (Boolean) Whether the item was discovered automatically.
- `id` (Number) NetBox id.
- `label` (String) Physical label.
- `last_updated` (String)
- `manufacturer_id` (Number) Id of the manufacturer.
- `name` (String)
- `owner_id` (Number) Id of the owner the object is assigned to.
- `parent_id` (Number) Id of the parent inventory item.
- `part_id` (String) Manufacturer part number.
- `role_id` (Number) Id of the inventory item role.
- `serial` (String) Serial number.
- `status` (String) Operational status. One of: offline, active, planned, staged, failed, decommissioning.
- `tags` (Set of String) Slugs of the tags assigned to the object (the provider's default_tags are added on top, see tags_all).
- `tags_all` (Set of String) Slugs of all tags on the object, including the provider's default_tags.
- `url` (String)
